findings.description: SYS-SUP-037 requires a start-up reset-cause message after classification but gives no deadline. An observer cannot determine when the obligation has failed. OP-SYS-001 defers the missing deadline to software requirements.

SYS-SUP-029, SYS-SUP-030, SYS-SUP-064 and SYS-SUP-065 condition the response on there being no 60 s of fault-free operation since the first detection. SYS-SUP-059 clears a count only after 60 s since the most recent detection of any code. Detections at 0, 59 and 118 seconds can therefore leave the count at three while failing the third-detection condition, contrary to CON-SUP-140.
findings.requested_change: Align the reset and latch conditions with the per-code count and the fault-free interval specified by CON-SUP-135 and CON-SUP-140.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-061 prohibits entering the safe state because of a code 8 report, while SYS-SUP-065 sets the latch on the third code 8 report and SYS-SUP-070 holds the outputs in the safe state while latched. CON-SUP-130 says the report does not by itself enter the safe state, but also counts toward the latch rule.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the code 8 start-up behavior so that the ordinary report and the third-detection latch case have consistent obligations.
